titles: Developing evidence-based care pathways for chronic disease in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to inform and influence China's national and local health policies, by developing and implementing evidence-based guidance for care pathways in terms of chronic disease management, to improve and standardise quality of care. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Building capacity for community-based dementia care in Qingdao, China
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK experience to inform forthcoming guidance on "Promoting Community Aged Care" in Qingdao, and policies under the 13th Five-Year Aged Care Plan in Qingdao, by June 2017. This will be done through study reports and capacity building. A comparative report on UK and Qingdao dementia care services is also being produced, which will be used to inform a public education campaign and policy recommendations. This will include proposals for a dementia care service model at the community level. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting sustainable urbanisation in Kunming, China
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise in urban regeneration to inform Kunming government policy, by adopting policy recommendations (for example, on urban planning and regeneration, and in the digital and healthcare fields). It is further intended that the Kunming government will disseminate best practice from Kunming-Liverpool co-operation, as a result of the ‘3 year cooperation plan' being implemented and commercial links established by this project. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Improved absorption and management of waste water at airports in China
descriptions: The project is designed to raise awareness of water management around major infrastructure projects through environmentally friendly designs. The primary focus will be Beijing's New Airport. The aim will be to help reduce the environmental impact, flood risks and minimise water consumption. The successful format can be used as a case study to repeat at other new airports and infrastructure developments ensuring efficient resource use and a reduced impact to surrounding populations.

titles: Improving educational equipment standards in China
descriptions: The project is designed to systematically analyse UK and Chinese education technology and equipment standards, and determine comparative advantage. This is intended to inform China's amendment of its education equipment standards for its 13th Five-Year Plan. It is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses including from the UK.

titles: Supporting China's educational reform and facilitate UK-China education cooperation
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK experience to deepen China's education reform and facilitate UK-China education cooperation. It will do this through setting up an education system pilot project in the fields of tourism and hospitality management, and cultural creativity, by June 2017. In doing so, it is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing a China Future School Assessment Guide to improve Chinese students' attainment and teachers' ability.
descriptions: The project is designed to use UK leading models of student and teaching assessment to trial and evaluate the UK assessment model in Chinese schools. This has the aim of establishing assessment standards for students and teachers, leading to China's Ministry of Education incorporating the standards proposed.

titles: Promoting the commercialisation of abandoned mine methane (AMM) recovery in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to produce a policy framework for an abandoned mine methane commercial pilot, which will be shared with key policy makers and stakeholders in China (including coal companies). The project will bring together UK and Chinese companies, enabling further pilots in China, and the potential for commercial opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Improving understanding of the risks for investors and implications for policymakers of stranded coal-fired power assets in China
descriptions: The project is designed to: (i) improve the understanding of financial institutions and regulators in China (such as the People's Bank of China and the China Banking Regulatory Commission) so they better understand the risks of stranded coal-fired generation assets and their precise exposure, so that they can shift capital away from such investments and take steps to manage the build-up of stranded asset risk in China's financial system; and (ii) support China's central government (e.g. the National Energy Administration and the National Development and Reform Commission) and the Jilin Provincial Government to better manage the political challenges, especially those in the electricity sector, associated with asset stranding and to formulate policies that can ensure a smoother transition away from coal-fired generation.

titles: Developing a framework to analyse structural reform, to support China's economic transition – and improve the G20 structural reform analysis framework
descriptions: This project is designed to improve the G20 structural reform analysis framework, particularly the quantitative analysis framework, and further improve the G20 structural reform agenda and assessment of reform efforts.

titles: Improving the capacity of clinical microbiologists in China against the global threat of antimicrobial resistance
descriptions: The project is designed to use UK expertise in clinical microbiology, to improve the capacity of clinical microbiologists in China. It is intended that antimicrobial stewardship will be implemented in China by March 2017.

titles: Building capacity and expertise for digital healthcare in Xi'an district, China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on experience and best practice from Sheffield to build capacity and expertise for digital healthcare in Xi'an and Tongchuan in China. The UK-China collaboration will focus on digital healthcare innovation, in order to build expertise and create links with key stakeholders in China's digital healthcare market, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Researching better hospital support for integrated medical and social care for the elderly in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise, through a series of UK-China collaborative activities, on integrated care research and development. It will include study reports and capacity building. This will help inform policy recommendations for China's National Committee on Ageing and the Ministry of Health in view of developing an improved integrated system for elderly requiring healthcare in China. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Promoting China's low carbon transition by mitigating the social and economic impacts of coal subsidy reform
descriptions: The project is designed to share UK and international experience to support China's National Development and Reform Commission's implementation of policies to mitigate the social and economic impacts of coal subsidy reform in China, to reduce its use of coal and coal subsidies in order to accelerate its low carbon transition. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Increasing renewable energy in China through developing policies on market models for supporting energy storage
descriptions: The project is designed to develop policies to support suitable market models for energy storage in China based on international best practice, enabling greater utilisation of renewable energy and creating new market opportunities in China's low carbon energy sector by June 2017, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Improving the credit bond rating system in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK experience to improve the current credit bond rating system in China, to strengthen exchanges and cooperation between the bond markets in China and the UK, and to support the process of RMB internationalization. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Support the development of China's cross-border e-commerce regulatory framework in the Guangdong Free Trade Zone
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on the best practice of UK e-commerce providers and government, to propose an innovative cross-border e-commerce regulatory approach, and support Guangdong Free Trade Zone. A clarification and harmonisation of rules as well as increased efficiency and transparency of its customs clearance, inspection and quarantine, will boost consumer confidence and encourage growth of local businesses. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development and impact of environmental, social and governance regulations through engagement with Chinese listed companies
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to raise awareness and capacity on climate reporting amongst the top 100 Chinese companies; assist the China Securities Regulatory Commission to accelerate its regulation on environmental, social and governance; and mainstream corporate climate change reporting in China.

titles: Helping China's G20 Presidency to promote women's entrepreneurship
descriptions: The project is designed to facilitate China's G20 Presidency driving forward the further development of women's entrepreneurship education programmes, to increase women's economic participation in the long term.

titles: Establishing a Carbon Capture Utilisation Storage initiative to accelerate policy formulation, technology and knowledge transfer in China.
descriptions: The project is designed to use UK expertise to establish the initial operation of the Beijing Carbon Capture Utilisation Storage (CCUS) Initiative; accelerate the policy-making process in China's National Development Reform Committee; enable technology and knowledge transfer; and help facilitate commercialisation of CCUS demonstration projects in China by March 2017.

titles: Tackling energy conservation and environmental policy conflicts in Guangdong, China
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Guangdong government, by the end of 2016, to take action to coordinate and integrate its currently segmented energy conservation and environmental policies. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones

titles: Helping Chinese G20 Presidency contribute to global governance
descriptions: The project, which involves the co-organisation of a forum by Chatham House and China's Counsellors Office of the State Council Forum, is designed to identify any remaining opportunities within G20 processes in the run up to the summit in Hangzhou in September 2016, and identify areas where UK-China cooperation could support the implementation of existing and new G20 agreements on global governance following the summit.

titles: Capacity building in cities in East China, to help China's industrial upgrade and sustainable economic growth
descriptions: The project is designed to support China's industrial upgrade and the sustainability of China's economic model. It intends to do this through new strategic collaborations between six cites in the Midlands (through the Midlands ‘Engine for Growth') and cities in East China. These collaborations will be in areas such as automotives, healthcare, creativity, financial services, education and manufacturing and are expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Promoting best practice on the green and low-carbon development of "Characteristic Small Towns" suggested by China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK experience to support China's Ministry of Housing and Urban and Rural Development to adopt green and low carbon policies and technologies in its planning for "Characteristic Small Towns". The envisaged timetable is for the Ministry to issue Case Studies, Policies and Assessment Methodologies by June 2017. Then for three small towns in China to adopt the policies, technologies and best practices by March 2017. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing transport connectivity in China's City Cluster in the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River
descriptions: The project is designed to use policies and best practice from the UK's Northern Powerhouse to develop transport connectivity in China's City Cluster in the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River. By June 2017, it is intended that the National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Transport and Wuhan government will adopt integrated physical and digitally connected transport planning polices and measures, that reflect UK expertise. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing capacity in China's cultural heritage sector and transition to a service-led economy, creating openings for UK and international business
descriptions: The project is designed draw on UK expertise to provide, by Feb 2017, capacity building to improve skills levels in China's museums sector in the target areas of curation and management. The project is also designed to promote UK-China collaborations and inform recommendations for policy approaches that can be implemented at a national level to improve commercial and creative sustainability in the sector. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting policy development for Chinese Free Trade Zones
descriptions: The project is designed to introduce the UK's experience, by enabling the authorities of the Pilot Free Trade Zones (FTZs) in China to increase their knowledge of administering the FTZs and improve their policies on trade, investment, finance and business models in the Zones.

titles: Supporting development of policy in Hubei to facilitate the competitiveness of heavy industry transiting to a new National Emissions Trading Scheme
descriptions: The project is designed to develop policy recommendations to support the Hubei government's allocation of carbon credits to companies in a way that protects industrial competitiveness, helping pave the way for a sustainable national carbon market in China. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the economic transition of China's Northeast region through innovation, particularly in the field of intelligent and advanced manufacturing
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to promote innovation in Northeast China, particularly in the advanced manufacturing sector. It is intended that government officials, research institutions and businesses from Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang and Inner Mongolia provinces, and the National Development and Reform Commission, will draw on UK experience. This will result in greater local collaboration and the effective implementation of policies that encourage innovation, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Strengthening skills and Intellectual Property protection in the creative sector in Jiangsu, China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK Intellectual Property expertise to introduce stakeholders in Jiangsu to best international practices in film and TV co-production, and prepare Jiangsu's practitioners to work at a strategic, global level with enhanced protection of intellectual property. Jiangsu's film and TV makers will build their knowledge and skills to help create an expanding and sustainable sector. The project will help to facilitate collaboration between the UK and Jiangsu on film and TV cooperation, generating opportunities between China and international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Embedding international standards for the ethical use of research on animals in China.
descriptions: The project is designed to encourage collaboration between UK and Chinese scientists, so that by 2018 there will be UK-China compatibility of animal welfare standards, as well as an ethical review, developed in collaboration with the China Rural Technology Development Centre, the Chinese Association for Laboratory Animal Sciences and the Development Research Centre of the State Council. Revised Chinese regulations and standards of animal welfare will meet international standards and subsequently significantly promote scientific collaborations between China and international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting China to join the OECD Mutual Acceptance of Data system to reduce unnecessary animal testing
descriptions: The project is designed to strengthen China's domestic institutions (Ministries, etc) through harmonisation with international data acceptance standards for the testing of human medicines in animals. This will remove trade barriers, improving China's economic development and ease of access to internationally (including UK) produced pharmaceuticals, and end expensive and unnecessary duplication of animal testing. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international pharmaceutical businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting Chinese local government adoption of sustainable urban development models
descriptions: The project is designed to: (1) support Chinese local governments adoption of sustainable urban development models in their policy making on ‘Smart Cities' and ‘Sponge Cities' by using UK expertise and experience demonstrated in a road show; (2) support China's urban planners and developers to take the UK's low-carbon principles and specific know-how on low-carbon city development, and build city partnerships between the two countries. The collaboration is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Enhancing the growth of China's financial markets by developing cooperation models
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance the growth of China's financial markets and add a futures element to the Shanghai-London Stock Connect, by proposing several options for cooperation models to the China Securities Regulation Commission, and demonstrating the suitability and feasibility of each model to the international and British market by the end of March 2017.

titles: Enhancing cooperation in order to upgrade the capacities of China's regulatory and supervisory authorities
descriptions: The project is designed to establish a mechanism for regular cooperation and dialogue between the UK and Chinese financial regulatory authorities - at working level, and in support of senior/VIP visits. It is also intended to lay the ground for long-term systematic financial cooperation between UK and China, in order to upgrade Chinese capacity in these areas.

titles: Harmonising civil nuclear standards between China and the UK, in support of the delivery of China's 13th Five-Year Plan
descriptions: The project is designed to harmonise civil nuclear standards between China and the UK through more mutual recognition. It will involve China's implementation of an adoption process, supporting structural reform, thereby reducing Greenhouse gas emissions, increasing energy security and providing opportunities for international businesses (including UK ones) in bilateral and third market trade and investment.

titles: Improving flood control in Shanghai, China
descriptions: The project is designed to support the design and evaluation of policies and strategies for flood risk reduction and disaster prevention in Shanghai through exchange of expertise and best practice. It will also provide scientific data and advice on simulation tools to improve Shanghai's sustainable urban planning.

titles: Supporting the improvement of the maritime arbitration service in Fujian Free Trade Zone, China
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Fujian Free Trade Zone (FTZ) to issue policy, by the end of 2017, to release market access barriers for international companies in the field of commercial maritime legal service through the successful development of a new pilot in maritime arbitration policy and services. UK experience and best practice will be drawn upon to improve the capacity of Chinese stakeholders in the field of commercial maritime legal services, facilitating market access for international companies, including UK businesses, into the Fujian FTZ maritime legal services industry.

titles: Facilitating sustainable agriculture development in China through enhanced sharing of knowledge
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to help China develop a comprehensive information sharing platform for promoting sustainable agriculture. This will improve information flow and openness among industries, academics and governments, and is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses including UK ones.

titles: Identifying Carbon Capture Utilisation and Storage development opportunities in Xinjiang, China
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Xinjiang Autonomous Region Development and Reform Commission to systematically assess and identify regional Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS) development opportunities, and build capacity for CCUS development in Xinjiang.

titles: Supporting the amendment of China's renewable energy law, to remove roadblocks to renewable energy development
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise so that, by March 2017, a bill is proposed to the National People's Congress, and legislative support is secured, for advancing key amendments to the Renewable Energy Law into China's 2018-2023 National Legislation Plan. The amendments are designed to mitigate bottlenecks slowing the development of China's renewable energy sector, in which international businesses, including UK ones, are accessing business opportunities.

titles: Incentivising waste utilisation in infrastructure delivery in Wuhan, China
descriptions: The project is designed to impart UK lessons on cross-industry utilisation of waste, to produce policy recommendations which are implemented by Wuhan Development Reform Commission. The recommendations will incentivise circular economy practices in the construction industry to utilise waste. This would generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Increasing levels of international best practice in technology transfer in Guangdong
descriptions: The project is designed to create a highly-skilled and strongly-networked cohort of Chinese technology transfer professionals who will share UK and international technology transfer practice in Guangdong province and more widely through China, generating opportunities for international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Supporting the implementation of China's National Action Plan on tackling antimicrobial resistance, by educating health workers
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to support the Chinese government's adoption of best practice and proposals on a comprehensive implementation plan to establish suitable antimicrobial resistance (AMR) education and training programmes. The project will also develop AMR stewardships for healthcare students and healthcare professionals across China, a key area within China's National Action Plan on AMR.

titles: Developing China's Museum infrastructure in order to increase the potential for international collaboration
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance the sustainable development of museums across China through international collaboration involving policy makers, decision makers and professionals, leading to stronger business development skills that result in a more sustainable cultural sector. This is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting RMB internationalisation through issuing RMB-denominated infrastructure bonds in London, for China's One Belt One Road Initiative
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise for a policy presentation to UK and Chinese authorities, which will provide policy analysis and recommendations on how issuance of infrastructure finance bonds in the London Offshore market could expand the international use of China's RMB currency and support the objectives of China's One Belt One Road Initiative.

titles: Building capacity in China's cultural sector, supporting China's transition to a service led economy and its engagements with international markets
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to enhance China's cultural heritage sector through international collaboration involving policy makers, decision makers and professionals. It will involve conducting research, and running training programmes and study visits, in partnership with China's State Administration of Cultural Heritage and its Ministry of culture; and promoting UK-China collaborations. In doing so, it will develop and improve capabilities and skill levels of cultural heritage professionals. It will address some of the economic and social pressures facing Chinese cultural heritage driven by climate change, natural disasters, environmental changes and tourism development. The project is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Building capacity of China's clothing design industry, helping China transition to a service led economy and its engagement with international markets
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to support economic reform in China's clothing and design industry through increased international collaboration involving industry professionals, associations and policy makers, making it more capable of operating in international markets. This will support the Chinese transition to a more service-orientated economy, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Building the capacity of China's Information and Communications Technology industry, including through best practice in intellectual property policy
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance China's Information and Communications Technology (ICT) industry through skills development and increased international collaboration between industry professionals, associations and policy makers, making it more capable of operating in international markets. This will support the Chinese transition to a more service-oriented economy and is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing offshore RMB centres to accelerate China's internationalisation policy for its RMB currency
descriptions: The project is designed to develop offshore Renminbi (RMB) centres by increasing issuance of RMB-denominated bonds in global foreign exchange trade centres, pushing forward the innovation of RMB-denominated financial derivatives.

titles: Supporting China's City Clusters policy development and implementation
descriptions: The project is designed to establish a structured partnership between UK and China on City Cluster collaboration that supports China in adopting UK sustainable urban development principles and policies. This has the potential to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Connecting China and the UK on the ‘One Belt One Road' (OBOR) initiative to enhance the sustainability and inclusiveness of OBOR projects
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance the understanding of beneficiary countries in Central and South Asia of China's One Belt One Road vision, and identify several socioeconomic and commercially viable cooperation projects involving China, the UK and beneficiary countries in the China Pakistan Economic Corridor. This will increase inclusive and sustainable development in the countries along the routes, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Facilitating Chinese cities' sustainable development by developing a guideline for China's urban regeneration planning
descriptions: The project is designed to introduce and incorporate UK concepts of regeneration into China's Ecological Restoration and Urban Regeneration Initiative, by its Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, facilitating the development of more sustainable regeneration methodologies in Chinese cities. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of China's technological innovation infrastructure
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance China's technology innovation environment through collaborative between China-UK companies. A UK-China TechHUB Boot Camp programme will help up skill local capability and capacity, provide examples of international expertise and best practice, as well as acting as a signpost mechanism for local funding sources, business and providers.

titles: Supporting China's Free Trade Zone and supply side structural reform
descriptions: The project is designed to provide comprehensive guidance to the Chinese government to help influence policy in furthering trade and investment within the Free Trade Zones (Tianjin and Guangdong in particular). The project also aims to help influence new supply side structural reforms that focus on cutting low-end supply while increasing high-end supply of goods and services by stimulating business through tax cuts, entrepreneurship and innovation. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Promoting the healthy development of emerging industries in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK experience to design and deliver training programmes on emerging industries to at least 160 senior government officials/business leaders. This will enhance their capabilities to develop innovation policies for emerging industries in China, whose implementation is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones

titles: Improving China's urban city environment through operationalising the UK-China Urbanisation Platform
descriptions: The project is designed to ensure the UK-China Urbanisation Platform enters into full operation, in support of the UK-China City Cluster Overarching Partnership, and the UK-China Smart Cities Partnership, as well as planning in China. This will improve China's urban city environment and liveability by supporting the Chinese government's development of relevant policies, whose implementation is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of Smart Cities policy in China
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Chinese government on Smart City policy development using UK's Smart City standard and experiences, creating opportunities for international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Foster green growth in China by addressing overcapacity in the steel and shipbuilding sectors through industrial restructuring and upgrading
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Chinese government to incorporate international best practices in cleaning up heavy and highly polluting industries, and ensure decisive actions are taken to address excess capacity in the steel and shipbuilding sectors. This will incorporate a green growth perspective.

titles: Strengthening primary care capacity in by training of practitioners in paediatrics to help China's economic development and the health of its poor.
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to strengthen the training of Chinese GPs in paediatrics to improve their skills across diagnoses and treatments, in pilot cities. This project will enable primary care institutions to take on more responsibilities in dealing with child medical issues, relieving pressure on tertiary paediatric services. Chinese policy makers will use the pilot report to inform the establishment of tiered treatment guidelines. This is expected to generate commercial and collaborative opportunities for international entities, including UK ones.

titles: Impact assessment of strategic programme fund projects conducted in China
descriptions: An impact assessment to establish the successful impacts and outcomes from previous strategic programme activity in China, helping to identify opportunities for future interventions.

titles: Supporting the development of the New Energy Vehicle industry in China
descriptions: The project is designed to share UK experience to support the development of the New Energy Vehicle Industry in China: firstly, on policies and incentives for charging facilities; secondly, on innovation and technology in vehicles. It is intended that recommendations will be put forward to the Chinese authorities proposing detailed planning of charging facilities and adoption of a technology roadmap. If taken up by China, international businesses, including UK ones, will be in a better position to understand Chinese policies and identify trade and investment opportunities.

titles: Supporting China's strategic development of its technology and satellite industries to promote international innovation and collaboration
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to support China's development of a roadmap that identifies specific challenges and opportunities in its emerging technology and satellites industries. This will include supporting China's strategic development of satellite applications and data management and sharing mechanisms. China's technology and satellite industries are ones that underpin almost all of China's development priorities, including agriculture, health care, climate change, monitoring air pollution, and urban development. The project is intended to open international, academic, industrial and government collaboration. It supports China's intention to move to a sustainable economic model led by innovation, in line with China's Five-year plan. It is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Introduce best practices on the development of Public and Private Partnerships (PPPs) that benefit Colombian citizens
descriptions: To increase the professional capacity of the PPP Agency via the training of its members and for these professionals to be able to implement the PPP projects and programs to be developed by the City of Medellin. By this training and exposure to international projects, it is expected that the Agency will be in a better position to take the projects to market both at national and international level.

titles: Use of SMART technology to improve Bogota's mobility and facilitate institutional collaboration
descriptions: To contribute to the construction of a smarter Bogota by developing an implementation plan and actions based on the existing mechanisms and the UK experience to share key transport and mobility information and facilitating institutional collaboration, thereby expanding economic impact and increasing opportunities for international investment.

titles: Use of Big Data to strengthen urban development and public transport investment in Colombia
descriptions: Strengthening the economic impact of public transport investments in Colombian cities by pioneering use of mobile phone data in Cali to inform urban development and public transport planning.

titles: Rehabilitation of mercury-contaminated mining lands in Colombia for renewable energy and other self-sustaining re-use strategies
descriptions: The project will support the rehabilitation of land affected by soil mercury pollution in disadvantaged areas in Colombia, bringing the land back into productive use focusing on renewable energy opportunities and/or other services as most appropriate. It will do this by providing a range of science based strategies that will support greater regional stability, harness low carbon innovation and identify opportunities for new community enterprise.

titles: Roadmap for public-private participation in the forthcoming Green Growth Mission of Colombia
descriptions: To develop a roadmap for public-private participation in the Green Growth Mission of Colombia and improve Colombia's competitiveness by increasing private sector understanding and leadership on green growth as part of the OECD agreements for a resilient-low carbon economy.

titles: Enhancing the capability of Colombia to regulate offshore oil and gas major accident hazard
descriptions: To enable the Colombian government regulators to implement a regulatory framework that reflects international best practice in the regulation of offshore major accident safety hazards, thereby making the sector more appealing to international investment.

titles: Catalysing energy efficiency in the Colombian industrial sector: boosting waste heat recovery, optimization of processes, replacement of boilers
descriptions: The project will evaluate energy efficient opportunities and help implement the most effective technologies for heat recovery (modern boilers ) and improve industrial processes. This will be scaled up through financing opportunities (specially design loans) , further helping to accelerate Colombia's transition to a low carbon economy.

titles: New technologies for waste treatment and energy generation that helps accelerate Colombia's transition to a low carbon economy
descriptions: This project will accelerate Colombia's transition to a low carbon economy by identifying the most feasible, and environmentally friendly methods and technologies suitable for waste treatment and energy generation, enabling to divert more of the residual waste that still exist away from the landfill and to capture renewable energy, and also, ensuring that the residual waste being used has the right renewable content and is matched with a plant that is efficient enough at converting waste to energy.

titles: Introduce sustainable waste management to the Pacific Region of Colombia delivering a model that can be replicated across the country
descriptions: Introduce sustainable waste management systems in Guapi and Nuqui, and develop a toolkit that can be used by other Municipalities in Colombia. The project's primary aim will be to address the urgent need to put in place appropriate waste collection and disposal measures whilst, in parallel, developing a medium term strategy focused on improving recycling/composting and treatment of residual waste to reduce landfill disposal. UK expertise will be showcased to main decision makers in the region and at National Level through the Ministry of Housing and Presidency programmes for poverty alleviation.

titles: Promoting the development of smart grids by implementing Advanced Metering Infrastructure in Colombia
descriptions: The project will implement an Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) for the Colombian electricity sector; reducing losses (technical and non-technical ) , improving network planning and facilitating the integration of renewable technology for the most cost effective option.

titles: Scoping funds to support future development and welfare programming in Colombia
descriptions: Scoping project opportunities to deliver significant primary and secondary benefit in the following areas: Education; Health; Mining; Financial Services; Energy; and Business Environment and Trade.

titles: Unlocking economic opportunities in Colombia's post-conflict regions
descriptions: We will carry out four studies of research , the information and evidence is required to take important investment decisions during implementation of the full programme

titles: Scoping study for the future Global Trade Programme interventions relating to intellectual property
descriptions: Scoping study to identify the barriers to enforcing Intellectual Property Rigts (IPR) in targeted ODA-eligible countries and develop a programme supporting stronger protection of IPR. Improving the target counties ability to trade with the world (including UK), increasing their economic growth, employment and prosperity.

titles: Scoping study for the future Global Trade Programme interventions relating to regulatory reform
descriptions: v

titles: Scoping study for the future Global Trade Programme interventions relating to developing standards and quality of infrastructure
descriptions: Scoping study to identify the barriers to improving standard in infrastructure in targeted ODA eligible countries and develop programme interventions to adopt better standards and quality infrastructure. Improving the target counties ability to trade with the world (including UK), increasing their economic growth, employment and prosperity.

titles: Scoping study for the future Global Trade Programme interventions relating to customs procedures and standards
descriptions: Scoping study to develop a programme to support targeted ODA eligible countries access and deveop international trade opportunities. Identifying interventions to streamline customs procedures and standards and to tackle corruption at targeted seaports. Improving the target counties ability to trade with the world (including UK), increasing their economic growth, employment and prosperity.

titles: Scoping study in the Eastern Europe and Central Asia Region to provide analysis for possible future programme interventions
descriptions: This project is designed to provide analysis into potential programme activity aimed at improving the business environment in Ukraine, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Georgia and Turkmenistan. Looking at increased opportunities for businesses in the region, including from the UK.

titles: Scoping study to provide analysis for a low carbon energy transformation programme
descriptions: Scoping study to help develop an ODA-eligible programme to support and accelerate the low carbon energy transition in targeted developing countries. The study explores how to form and reform essential markets for low carbon transition, which are also areas of UK policy and commercial strength. This includes green finance, smart energy, and low carbon goods and services, and makes recommendations on how best to reduce poverty and realise secondary benefits for business.

titles: Scoping study to provide analysis for a global future cities programme
descriptions: This project will scope the opportunities available to improve the planning and management of cities for a future cities programme. Analysing how to improve living conditions by using UK and Global expertise to reduce urban overcrowding, pollution, congestion and inadequate basic services in ODA eligible countries.

titles: Establishing the South East Asian Marine Energy Centre in Indonesia to enable a long-term sustainable strategy for marine energy in SE Asia
descriptions: This project aims to create a regional centre of excellence for marine energy. The centre will bring together stakeholders using the ABCG model (Academic-Business-Communities-Government) to drive innovation. The centre will provide support for policy-making, build research and development partnerships and improve technical skills. By building regional capacity, it will drive development of the marine energy market in South East Asia,  generating business opportunities including for UK companies.

titles: Supporting regulatory reform by evaluating the implementation of business licensing deregulation in regions of Indonesia
descriptions: This project supports effective implementation of economic policy packages. It provided training on streamlining of business licensing and evaluated implementation in six major business cities in Indonesia. Streamlining will reduce costs to business, opening market opportunities including for UK companies.

titles: Producing a legal review to inform and analyse trade regulations in Indonesia, including on import-export procedures
descriptions: The project is designed to produce a legal review, to identify and analyse potential problems on trade-related regulations in Indonesia, particularly on export-import procedures, and provide recommendations and solutions for removing regulatory barriers to improve ease of doing business, resulting in benefit to businesses already trading with Indonesia as well as attracting new UK and international businesses to the market.

titles: Supporting the development of a regulatory framework for renewable energy independent power producers in Indonesia
descriptions: The project is designed to help Indonesia achieve its clean energy targets by supporting the development of a framework for a regulation on renewable energy independent power producers. This should lead to the generation of opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones, throughout the renewable energy supply chain (e.g. project management, engineering) and across sectors (e.g. marine, solar, geothermal) as the market in Indonesia develops.

titles: Promoting integrity and legal transparency in the Indonesian maritime sector
descriptions: The project is designed to promote integrity and legal transparency in the Indonesian maritime sector via a single point of contact at ports who will act as concierge for businesses and navigate the system on their behalf.  This will remove barriers such as facilitation payments, and improve the ease of doing business for UK companies operating in Indonesia. The project will specifically target the port of Tanjung Priok and one additional port in Indonesia, and build on the work and methodology from phase one of the project.

titles: Supporting Indonesia to develop its geothermal market, to assist the development of sustainable and clean energy
descriptions: The project is designed to assist the Indonesian Ministry of Energy develop revised geothermal policies that will stabilise and open up the geothermal market, increasing economic growth, reducing climate change emissions, and generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing the Indonesian government bond primary dealer system and the domestic currency government bond market.
descriptions: The project is designed to assist Indonesia's Ministry of Finance to develop a sound primary dealers system and recommend measures to promote the domestic repo markets. When implemented, the result is expected to be fairer, more transparent and robust Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) denominated government bond markets, which have improved liquidity and efficiency. This would result in lower systemic risk in the financial sector and accelerate the development of the Indonesian economy.

titles: Supporting the improvement of Public Sector Accounting Standards in Indonesia
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise through a Government Auditors & Finance Officer capacity building programme in International Public Sector Accounting Standards, in order to align public sector accounting in Indonesia with international and UK standards. This will improve transparency and reduce corruption, enhancing the prospects for international and UK companies in public procurement and infrastructure projects.

titles: Supporting the enhancement of Indonesia's legal and institutional framework to counter corruption
descriptions: The project is designed to provide technical assistance to enhance the legal and institutional framework for fighting and preventing corruption affecting and involving the private sector in Indonesia. International businesses, including UK ones, are expected to benefit from this.

titles: Administrative costs of Prosperity Fund ODA projects in India
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in India.

titles: Pursuing reforms at Indian ports to improve the trading environment for international business.
descriptions: To improve India's trading environment by pursuing action points on bottlenecks in processes and procedures that increase the cost and time of doing trade, which were identified in the previous project on infrastructural deficiencies in Indian ports.

titles: Reducing transaction costs of India-UK trade by identifying and tackling problems for business in Indian Customs procedures.
descriptions: Work with India's Customs department and other key stakeholders to identify barriers, provide solutions to improve existing bottlenecks and build the capacity of Customs officials. This will reduce the transaction costs faced by international businesses including from the UK.

titles: Supporting implementation in India of the World Bank's anti-money laundering risk assessment framework
descriptions: Identify, assess and understand the problems caused by money laundering within India, using the World Bank's Risk-Based Approach methodology, and suggest appropriate mitigation measures. Resulting improved business environment will benefit domestic and international businesses.

titles: Lowering trade costs and improving the business environment in India
descriptions: Assessing procedural and infrastructural constraints to trade in India and identifying ways to facilitate trade and improve the business environment, including learning from best practices in UK. An improved business environment will benefit foreign businesses operating in India.

titles: Promoting business reform in India's states to the ‘Ease of Doing Business' requirements of business.
descriptions: This project will provide real time feedback on the effectiveness of business reforms being implemented across states with a special focus on reforms in tax policy and administration, construction permits and regulatory and inspection reforms. The recommendations will help improve the business climate in states, leading to reduced red tape for international businesses.

titles: Aligning India's e-governance policies and practices to global standards
descriptions: Aligning India's e-governance policies and practices to global standards by building capacity on digital governance, with a focus on the state of Maharashtra. This will equip the officers with necessary skills and knowledge to enhance operational efficiency in administration and service delivery leading to improved government interaction with foreign businesses.

titles: Strengthening India-UK partnership on regulatory and inspection reforms
descriptions: The project builds on previous engagement with the Government of India and delivers an intensive capacity building programme to enhance the capacity of central and State Government officials on regulatory reforms, designing regulatory and risk assessment frameworks. Resulting improved business environment will benefit domestic and international businesses.

titles: Developing approaches for improving the business environment in India
descriptions: Support India's 'ease of doing business' work by building capacity within Indian Government Departments and States. In particular, share expert knowledge and experience from the UK to help India develop approaches for improving the business environment that will benefit domestic and international firms.

titles: Promoting UK best practices on e-governance in India to enhance service delivery and transparency in public bureaucracy
descriptions: Identify areas in which HMG can assist the Government of India in improving e-governance practices. The project will assess India's e-governance processes and identify areas to improve digital governance, administrative capability and public sector reforms. A uniform IT framework will enhance service delivery benefitting domestic and international firms.

titles: Supporting the Competition Commission of India to promote an international rules-based regulatory climate for businesses
descriptions: Improve market competition in India by building capacity of the regulatory authority through training/education on the application of economics in competition. Increased capacity will lead to a more stable business environment, benefiting domestic and international businesses.

titles: Supporting ease of doing business engagement in India on taxes, trade facilitation, land registry and e-governance
descriptions: HMG experts to assess India's performance on key indicators of the Ease of Doing Business Index such as paying taxes, trade facilitation, land registry and e-governance and recommend better practices. The recommendations, once implemented, will improve India's business environment and benefit both domestic and international businesses.

titles: Accelerating India's transition to gas by enabling increased market access
descriptions: Catalyse a faster transition to a gas based economy in India for increased energy security, trade and lower carbon emissions. This will be achieved through the sharing of international regulatory best practices and the creation of the India Gas Forum to promote engagement between industry and government.

titles: Accelerating the use of green bonds to raise international capital for India's sustainable economic growth.
descriptions: To support the listing of green bonds by Indian issuers in the City of London, raising international capital to finance low-carbon and climate resilient projects in India.

titles: Creating an Energy Conservation Fund in India to drive industrial energy efficiency and stimulate the market for international businesses
descriptions: To support the Government of India in designing and operationalising an Energy Conservation Fund, based on the experience of the UK's Carbon Trust, that will catalyse investment in industrial energy efficiency and open commercial opportunities.

titles: Developing up the industrial energy efficiency market in India.
descriptions: Scale up the energy efficiency market in India by bringing industry and policy makers together to shape policy, share best practice and access UK and international expertise. This will contribute to increased energy security, sustainable economic growth and international commercial partnerships.

titles: Supporting Indian legislators to implement clean energy technologies and promote low carbon development at the local level.
descriptions: Increase the take up of low carbon solutions by supporting legislators to deliver clean energy plans at local level including through policy reforms and building their links with industry. Scaled up deployment will support international climate commitments and commercial opportunities for clean energy.

titles: Building India's energy storage market to support energy security and low carbon growth
descriptions: Support international collaboration and commercial partnerships on energy storage technology in order to grow the Indian market and support India to achieve its renewable energy targets by sharing approaches, business models and innovation.

titles: Helping Indian cities manage climate risks.
descriptions: This project aims to help Indian cities understand the climate induced risks they face and the policy, investment and insurance related responses to address these risks. As well as creating demand for climate risk management services, improved understanding will lead to infrastructure opportunities that are more sustainable, making them more attractive to domestic and international investors.

titles: Supporting India to prepare for its first offshore wind farm.
descriptions: This project will help India to attract international investors, project developers and supply chains for development of its off-shore wind sector, through analytical work on the tariff, policy and regulatory conditions needed to make the first offshore wind project investable.

titles: Disaster proofing Indian cities by strengthening delivery of emergency services during climate extremes.
descriptions: This project will identify additional services/equipment needed to more effectively deliver emergency services during climate extreme events in Indian cities, build capacity of emergency services operators and increase awareness of supply chain companies (including internationally) on specific Indian market needs and opportunities.

titles: Supporting smart city leadership and standards as enablers for smarter, resilient and more sustainable Indian cities.
descriptions: Support Indian cities to adopt internationally recognised policies and standards for smart and resilient development using the Smart City Leadership knowledge exchange programme. This will enable international companies, including from the UK, to effectively participate in Indian smart city programmes.

titles: Boosting corporate demand for low carbon goods and services in India through business commitments to renewable energy and energy efficiency.
descriptions: Grow the demand (and therefore inject momentum into the market) for low carbon technology and services by securing commitments from Indian businesses to increase their use of renewable energy and improve their energy efficiency. As well as a larger market the project will help India meet its international climate commitments.

titles: Supporting India to meet its CO2 emissions reductions ambitions.
descriptions: Assess India's power generation trends in relation to its development agenda and its use of domestic energy resources. Support India to assess options to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the power sector in support of its domestic and international commitments on climate change.

titles: Maximising impacts and benefits of future low carbon and energy projects in India
descriptions: Enhance the impact of future Prosperity Fund projects in India by increasing awareness of, and access to, knowledge generated and lessons learned for the government, project implementers and businesses.

titles: Supporting solar market growth in India.
descriptions: Accelerate the deployment of roof-top solar projects in two States in India by sharing UK best practice and supporting preparation of investable projects for Government and institutional buildings, which will grow the renewable energy market and make projects more attractive, including to international investors.

titles: Scoping study on climate risk insurance with a focus on 5 India-UK partnership cities.
descriptions: The project will identify and estimate the value of appropriate risk management services for Indian cities. This will help to encourage India's city managers to adopt climate risk management measures and support service providers, including from the UK, to shape their service offerings to suit the market.

titles: Preparing for the India-UK Energy for Growth Dialogue
descriptions: Identify key areas where UK-India collaboration can support India's electricity distribution reforms and grow the green finance and green technology sectors, supporting India's economic development and creating opportunities for international companies, including from the UK.

titles: Supporting the internationalisation of the Indian Rupee
descriptions: To produce an action plan for internationalisation of the Indian Rupee by sharing UK expertise, thereby laying out a clear roadmap for implementation by the Government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). An internationalised currency will support India's economic growth by creating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Promoting economic growth by sharing global expertise to develop India's overseas masala bond market.
descriptions: To increase access to finance in India by sharing international expertise on rupee based financing through foreign investors and sharing global examples, including from the city of London. This will benefit Indian firms as they gain better access to international markets like London, thereby creating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Analysis of India's Financial Technology sector for the India UK Financial Partnership.
descriptions: Provide a detailed analysis of the market and growth trends of India's Financial Technology industry, assess its alignment with the Government of India's economic policies and consider how the UK can support India's fintech evolution. A vibrant fintech market that attracts international players will support India's economic growth and development.

titles: Promoting the UK Bribery Act in India through multilevel interventions.
descriptions: The project aims to raise awareness around the UK Bribery Act among the Indian stakeholders and British companies operating in India, including through a survey, seminars and conference. This aims to help address bribery as a constraint to growth and business activity.

titles: Developing India's pension sector to promote greater financial inclusion and create opportunities for international businesses including UK ones.
descriptions: Identifying areas of development in India's pension market and promoting collaboration between Indian and international organisations, including UK ones, resulting in the supply of pension assets that can safely fund long-term investment and deliver economic growth.

titles: Strengthen India-UK financial market collaboration and supporting development of India's corporate bond market.
descriptions: The project aims to share UK best practices and expertise in developing India's corporate bond market enabling Indian firms to attract domestic and international investors. A stronger bond market will support India's economic growth and create opportunities for Indian and International financial services firms.

titles: Supporting development of India's re-insurance market by leveraging UK expertise.
descriptions: Share best practice with the Indian insurance regulator to strengthen and further develop the insurance sector in India which will make India a more attractive place for international firms to do business.

titles: Support the effective implementation of India's new insolvency law.
descriptions: Sharing international best practices (including from the UK) to assist India's Insolvency Board implement India's new insolvency law. This will help provide faster resolution of bankruptcy cases and improve the ease of doing business in India thereby benefitting domestic and international businesses.

titles: Promoting alternative financing models and reforms to support the development of the infrastructure financing sector in India.
descriptions: Assessing procedural constraints and identifying ways to facilitate the development of the infrastructure financing sector, highlighting London as a partner for raising finance to meet India's financing needs.

titles: Builidng capacity within India's oil and gas sector
descriptions: Develop effective models for the delivery of training to enhance skills and create 'work-ready' employees for India's oil and gas sector, improving the labour supply in an area of commercial focus for the UK in India.

titles: Developing the vocational skills training capacity within India's construction sector
descriptions: Develop effective models for delivery of standardised construction training in three States. Standardisation benefits the sector, including international companies by helping to improve labour supply and capability as well as additional benefits such as improved safety. Standardisation also creates commercial opportunities for international training/curriculum providers.

titles: Increasing employment opportunities for disabled youth in India
descriptions: To support increased employment opportunities for India's disabled population through the development of English language training programmes for hearing impaired youth.

titles: Building capacity to improve India's paramedical training capabilities
descriptions: Scope, design and test effective models for the delivery of paramedical training in partnership with the state governments of Haryana, Punjab and Bihar, establishing UK expertise and standards in a sector of commercial focus (healthcare) for the UK in India.

titles: Scoping study assessing opportunities for greater engagement by the UK on skills development in India
descriptions: Scoping Study assessing opportunities for greater engagement by the UK on skills development in India. This will identify where the current constraints, challenges and opportunities lie, in view of better targeted future programme activity.

titles: Development and administration costs related to India Prosperity Fund Business Case
descriptions: Programme costs covering planning, implementation and resources for the development of the India Prosperity Fund programme

titles: Smart cities: Designing a national smart cities hub for India
descriptions: Support the Government of India to develop a blueprint and delivery framework for a National Smart Cities Hub in Pune, India. The hub will help promote sustainable urbanisation in India's cities by convening domestic and international stakeholders, including from the UK, in a single site to deliver commercial innovation activities.

titles: Development of a Transit Oriented Development (TOD) framework for India's smart cities
descriptions: Help the Government of India (GOI) deliver a national TOD framework to be adopted by state governments and related municipalities. TOD is a top GOI priority and there is huge demand in India's smart cities. The project will encourage the development of TOD projects to global standard, which is also likely to attract international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Supporting the Government of India's Smart Cities Mission and Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation.
descriptions: Work with the Government of India's Ministry of Urban Development to develop smart and sustainable urban projects that are viable commercial opportunities for international businesses, including those from the UK.

titles: Support the Government of Madhya Pradesh to develop Indore and other cities through India's Smart Cities and Atal Mission
descriptions: Support the State Government of Madhya Pradesh develop investible and sustainable projects in smart technology, solid waste management and e-governance. The urban projects will, in turn, also create commercial opportunities for international businesses, including those from the UK.

titles: Provide support and expertise on alternative infrastructure funding options to aid economic development in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India
descriptions: Support the State Government of Andhra Pradesh to access alternative revenue for urban development, including via raising bonds on the London Stock Exchange (LSE). This will help finance urban projects in the Greenfield city of Amaravati which attract international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Capacity building in urban transport infrastructure development for Amaravati
descriptions: Develop a transportation strategy for the Greenfield city of Amaravati. The project will scope out sustainable and cost-effective approaches in transportation, including via international best practices. The project will also provide a gateway for international technologies, including from the UK, to be commerically adopted and procured.

titles: Capacity building in the water supply and waste water management for Amaravati
descriptions: Develop a sustainable water management framework for the Greenfield city of Amaravati. The final framework will be used to implement a range of well-coordinated water projects, leading to better provisions for its citizens. The projects will, in turn, create commercial opportunities for international businesses, including those from the UK.

titles: Support the development of a Smart Infrastructure Masterplan in Pune
descriptions: Assist Pune to develop a Smart Infrastructure Master Plan for a future transit hub to be located outside the city. The master plan will incorporate international best practices in urban development. This is also likely to attract international businesses, including from the UK, during the subsequent implementation stage.

titles: Support to Pune Smart City Development Corporation Ltd (PSCDCL) in developing a start-up zone and transit hub
descriptions: Develop sustainable and feasible proposals for a start-up zone and transit hub outside the city of Pune. This will include market analysis, topographic surveying and site guidelines. The proposals will, in turn, create commercial opportunities for international businesses, including those from the UK

titles: Cities scoping study to assess the need and opportunities for greater engagement by the UK on urban development in India
descriptions: To understand the development constraints in India's cities and analyse the commerical potential in the sector, including specifically in the 20 lighthouse cities identified by the Government of India's Smart Cities Mission. The project will inform our future technical assistance programmes in urban developmnent.

titles: Build capacity in support of India's Housing for All (HfA) mission.
descriptions: Advisory support to Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation to develop sustainable and affordable housing models which draw on international best practices, including from the UK. The projects will, in turn, create commercial opportunities which may attract international businesses, including from the UK.

titles: Promote corporate governance and accountability programme in Kazakhstan
descriptions: Engaging with Kazakhstani stakeholders to develop a corporate governance and accountability programme for the financial sector to open up opportunities for Kazakhstan and international business.

titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects

titles: Establishing Monitoring and Evaluation mechanisms for the Cross-government Prosperity Fund
descriptions: To design and procure monitoring and evaluation systems for the Prosperity Fund. This will provide specialist skills to programmes and enable effective portfolio management at Fund level. We will use this system to help drive value for money and effective delivery of the Fund's objectives

titles: Supporting Malaysia to help meet its international climate change obligations
descriptions: The project is designed to establish an effective road map for the implementation of the Intended National Determined Contributions including the necessary readiness programme for the adoption of the Paris Agreement, hence providing an excellent opportunity for the UK to participate in strengthening institutional arrangements and capacities specifically in GHG inventory system, compliance reporting and prioritization of mitigation actions. It will do this by developing a set of strategic policy inputs and recommendations to the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment.

titles: Supporting Malaysia to establish a low carbon city and green growth strategy for Greater Kuala Lumpur
descriptions: The project is designed to catalyse low carbon transformation and green growth in key Greater Kuala Lumpur municipalities, by drawing on UK expertise to establish a low carbon city and green growth strategy and assist end-users in Malaysia and technology service providers to discuss project opportunities. This will assist sustainable development and is expected to generate opportunities for international and UK businesses in the low carbon sectors.

titles: Developing a strategic UK-Malaysia collaboration to internationalise the Malaysian Finance Sector
descriptions: The project is designed to support Malaysian ambitions to internationalise its Finance sector thereby building strong foundation and encouraging more international collaboration, particularly with UK players, through exploration in areas of co-operation. This will include creating a UK-Malaysia Finance working group focussing on key issues, including capital market development, fintech, insurance as well as broader financial and related professional services.

titles: Establishing a Policy Framework to scale up Combined Heat and Power deployment in Malaysia
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on local and international evidence to work with stakeholders in Malaysia and UK (including EPU, Energy Commission, Gas Malaysia, Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers, industries, equipment providers and banks) to demonstrate the opportunities for deployment of Combined Heat and Power in Malaysia and provide the evidence for the most favourable policy landscape to support this transition. This is expected to generate opportunities through the introduction of Malaysian stakeholders across major industry sectors to a wide range of UK equipment providers, consultants and innovators

titles: Supporting the development of transport solutions for Iskandar Regional Development Authority in Malaysia
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise in Smart Cities to support the Iskandar Region's sustainable transport policies and disseminate its results to other regions in Malaysia, mainly Melaka. This will assist the economic development of the southern business region in Malaysia and generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Improving Malaysia's business environment by tackling corruption and strengthening transparency
descriptions: The project is designed to create a more market-friendly business environment in Malaysia by increasing support for legal reforms needed to tackle corruption and by increasing the amount of information related to government procurement that is available to businesses and the public thereby encouraging business confidence to international companies including UK businesses

titles: Building the capacity of Malaysian law enforcement to tackle corruption
descriptions: The project is designed to build the capacity of Malaysian law enforcement through the conduct of a training programme that will increase the agencies' knowledge and ability in profiling and evaluating truth and credibility. This will ultimately change perceptions, improve market access and create a ‘levelled playing field' for international businesses, including UK ones, further addressing corruption's detrimental impact particularly on unfair business tendering or the smuggling of contraband, counterfeit goods.

titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects in Mexico
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in Mexico.

descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in Mexico.
