titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects in Mexico
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in Mexico.

titles: Promoting urban energy reform in Mexico
descriptions: This project will establish Knowledge Exchange Hubs between Mexico and the UK with the aim of improving social behaviour and quality of education on Smart Cities topics in line with Smart Cities best practices, whilst linking UK and Mexico SMEs, opening new opportunities for UK businesses to introduce new services and technology into the Smart Cities sector in Mexico.

titles: Developing Future Cities in Mexico through UK-Mexico Knowledge Exchange Hubs, boosting businesses through platforms for UK and Mexican SMEs
descriptions: This project establishes Knowledge Exchange Hubs between Mexico and the UK working with King's College London, the National University of Mexico (UNAM) and the Mexico City government organisation LabCDMX. The programme will improve social behaviour and quality in education in line with Smart Cities best practices within Mexico City by March 2017, as well as linking UK and Mexico SMEs in the priority areas of road traffic safety, mobility and air quality. In turn this is designed to open new opportunities for UK and other businesses to introduce new services and technology to this sector.

titles: Strengthen Mexico's capacity in the treatment of childhood cancer
descriptions: The project will improve the Mexican Healthcare System's decision making policies in line with Smart Cities solutions by granting people access to digital tools for early detection and treatment of childhood cancer. This digital platform will help gather the necessary information to identify the training and equipment needs for private and public hospitals, creating opportunities to introduce UK experience and technology into this area. It will map institutional capability and indentify priorities for long-term international investment.

titles: Improving Mexico's low carbon transportation systems
descriptions: The project will assist Mexico City's Government will improve the delivery of effective and efficient low carbon urban mobility solutions through adoption of smart transport innovations and data use, such as Integrated Transport Systems (ITS), real time traffic control centres, traffic safety interventions, passenger information systems and open data. This will open the market to UK and other technology providers for this sector.

titles: Support development of first comprehensive waste management strategy to improve Mexico's waste-to-energy and resource recovery capacity
descriptions: This pilot project in Guadalajara will support the development of the first comprehensive, cost-effective, and sustainable waste management strategy in Mexico , the second largest metropolitan area in the country, and generate a road map for waste-to-energy and other resource recovery projects. This will further open the fertile opportunities for international business in this sector across the country.

titles: Improving Mexico's ability to move to a low carbon economy through applying best practices
descriptions: The project will develop energy efficiency and other carbon reduction measures across buildings, vehicle fleets and operational activities in states by supporting the delivery of credible and robust Carbon Management Plans (CMPs). This project will open opportunities to UK and other businesses wishing to enter the market.

titles: Promoting Mexico's low carbon energy sector through the application of methodologies and tools.
descriptions: To mobilise investment and research capacity in clean technologies in Mexico by supporting the Mexican Ministry of Energy (SENER) and the Mexican Centres of Innovation and Energy (CEMIEs) to create a suite of methodological tools. This will help develop the clean technologies sector through engaging effectively with the private sector and prioritising technology-level initiatives. These new low carbon innovations will help unlock green growth and sustainable development in Mexico. This will also create opportuintiies for partnerships with UK research institutions and green technological start-ups.

titles: Supporting a low carbon economy in Mexico through the promotion of best practice in the energy efficiency of buildings
descriptions: The project aims to share UK best practice to empower Mexican cities to become low carbon hubs through the understanding of their main sources of emissions and simultaneously, offering them solutions in the implementation of the energy efficiency code in buildings. Greener cities will be beneficial both in terms of the health of residents and the general environment. It will create market opportunities for certification bodies and companies offering technological solutions including UK organizations.

titles: Building capability and capacity in Mexico for the future needs of the energy industry and a low carbon economy
descriptions: To design a set of strategies by March 2017 that will help the States of Campeche and Tamaulipas to have a roadmap for the development of the capability and capacity required by future market demands in the energy industry. This will improve the business environment in these states making it more attractive for international companies to do business there.

titles: Assessing the potential of biomass energy as part of Mexico's energy mix in support of a low carbon economy
descriptions: The project will assess potential cases for biomass energy production of new and existing processes in order to replace fossil fuels in Mexico, supporting the Ministry of Energy's development goals. It will identify potential synergies with UK and open opportunities for international companies with expertise and technology in this area to work in Mexico.

titles: Promoting innovative financing options to finance energy efficiency projects and help move Mexico to a low carbon economy
descriptions: Programme designed to foster the transition to a low-carbon economy, through the implementation of energy efficiency projects in areas related to health, education and/or other strategic public services. This project will also improve the Mexican economy and social welfare by boosting productivity and helping state governments to overcome budgetary constraints. Carbon Trust's list of trusted technology providers will bring opportunities for UK and other businesses to enter this sector.

titles: Developing a more effective oil and gas sector in Mexico by improving health and safety standards
descriptions: The project is designed to build capacity and with UK expertise improve the effectiveness of Mexico's Regulators on issues around major accident hazards in the energy sector. Improvement of health and safety standards in the offshore oil and gas (and the construction sector) in Mexico by March 2017. This will not only bring UK expertise and consultancy opportunities but will also improve the general business environment for UK businesses wishing to work in this crucial sector.

titles: Fostering local electricity generation for better energy supply in Mexico
descriptions: The project will prepare a "2030 distributed generation roadmap" to foster the development and adoption of public policy for distributed generation in Mexico and accelerate its use at residential, commercial, and small and medium-size company level. Distributed generation will have a positive impact on residental access to affordable energy, particuarly in marginalised regions currently lacking connectivity. It will also open up the Mexican market to global investment, including to UK best practice and experience as well as UK technologies to be used in the sector.

titles: Support improvement of Mexican regulation in the transportation and storage of hydrocarbons
descriptions: Through UK collaboration the project will support the Mexican Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) to improve regulation of transportation and storage of hydrocarbons, refined products and petrochemicals. This will facilitate the development of necessary infrastructure to support the creation of a competitive market and thus attract international investment.

titles: Improving Mexico's Energy Storage capacity to boost renewable energy integration and foster the transition to a low carbon economy
descriptions: The project will develop a framework to allow the building of energy storage capacity needed to integrate sources of renewable energy into the power grid effectively and achieve the Federal Government's clean energy goals in Mexico. This will also open up the renewable energy sector to UK and other businesses wishing to work in Mexico.

titles: Building capability and capacity in Mexico's oil and gas sector to maximise benefits of energy reform
descriptions: The project aims to build a comprehensive workforce development framework to address the skills gaps identified by the Ministry of Energy of Mexico (SENER). Using British expertise and experiences to ensure an improved business environment in the energy sector.

titles: Support improvement of English language teaching in Mexico's primary schools
descriptions: The aim of the project is to support Mexico's English Language strategy to become bilingual in 20 years through training 231 primary school teachers across 4 Mexican states to teach English to a high standard and train other teachers to do the same, and certifying them through Cambridge English Language Assessment. The outcome will be that the quality of English Language teaching in Mexico will have been enhanced, the Ministry of Education's capacity will have been increased in this area, and, in turn, the number of primary age pupils in Mexico's education system who have competence in the English language will have increased, starting with the 53,205 pupils taught by the trained teachers.

titles: Supporting educational reform in Mexico for an emerging market workforce
descriptions: The project will work with the Ministry of Education's Department of Secondary Technical Education to (a) develop new curricula for this level of education, (b) create a model 'makerspace' which can be used by technical students and which will inspire the creation of more such spaces; (c) train teachers and students in 'maker' education. The outcome will be that the secondary technical education system in Mexico will have its capacity increased and will be modernised to align with 21st century technologies, practices and needs.

titles: Developing education evaluation techniques in Mexico through UK expertise.
descriptions: The project will work with 28 schools across 3 states to develop manuals and tools designed to help each school to continuously evaluate its progress: including the quality of teaching, the performance of students and the performance of the school directors and administrators. It will develop these tools in close consultation with the schools themselves and with experts including Mexico's National Institute for Evaluation in Education (INEE), the British Council, OFSTED and the Education Development Trust. The outcome will be an overall improvement of quality in school performance in the affected schools through the creation of a culture of self-evaluation, which can in due course be rolled out more widely.

titles: Improving crime investigation by developing police technical capacities in the Mexican criminal justice system
descriptions: The project will provide federal, local and municipal police institutions in Mexico with specific guidelines and a methodology to continuously evaluate and improve their crime investigation capacities. The Police Development Unit of the National Security Commission will implement the methodology delivered by this programme in the states of Michoacán and Nuevo Leon.

titles: Promoting anti-corruption mechanisms in Mexican law enforcement agencies
descriptions: The project will develop a model to tackle corruption within the police at federal and state level. By the end of the project, three Memorandums of Understanding will be signed with State governors in order for them to commit to implement an anti-corruption model.

titles: Improving public safety in Mexico through community policing pilot
descriptions: The project will assist the Mexican government in the pilot implementation of the new Proximity Police Model. It will build capacity and provide learning for its future expansion, helping to reduce corruption and increase security

titles: Improving institutional responsibilities in the reformed system in Mexico by promoting anti-corruption measures
descriptions: Strengthening Mexican institutions to achieve maximum impact of the recently created National Anticorruption System. Key project activities comprise a mixture of: review of existing strategies, policies and procedures, bespoke capacity building and targeted consultancy activities to facilitate the implementation of the best practices endorsed. The proposed programme was requested to GovRisk by local stakeholder in order to ensure that a new Audit Quality Control Unit in accordance with international best practices, and a new best practice whistleblower system for public servants.

titles: Increasing transparency in Mexico through the use of an open data start-up hub
descriptions: The project will help deliver economic growth and transparency through data driven innovation. It will create simultaneous data innovation competitions in Mexico and the UK and connect businesses. Based on the proven model developed by the UK's Open Data Institute (ODI) and co-ordinated by the ODI, this project will establish an Open Data Startup Hub.

titles: Promoting prosperity through open government as part of the Open Government Partnership
descriptions: Helping three municipalities in Mexico develop the open government policy framework and implement its guidelines. PEGA ("Strategic Open Governance Plan") will be implemented in collaboration with leading actors to adapt ongoing international and national efforts of open government to local contexts and needs. It will dvelop effective mechanisms to create competitive cities through transparent and agile public institutions.

titles: Tackling corruption in Mexico through the introduction of digital procurement processes
descriptions: This project will provide the Mexican Government with a digital platform that will enable increased openness and transparency in the procurement process. As a result, procurement oversight will become increasingly independent. An accountability mechanism between government and citizens, targeted towards policy-makers, legislators, watchdogs, journalists, entrepreneurs, SMEs, international investors and risk analysts will be developed.

titles: Improving Mexico's capital markets by promoting new models in the crowdfunding markets
descriptions: Adopting UK models and using UK expertise into the Mexican crowdfunding market will increase access to finance for SME's building a more robust economy to meet new global challenges. The new financial solutions created will help improve the broader private capital markets in Mexico by March 2017.

titles: Improving Mexico's economic potential through greater understanding and use of Public-Private-Partnerships
descriptions: A diagnostic analysis of Mexico's Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) environment and guidelines to increase institutional awareness and capacity to support this financing method at regional, state and municipal levels. The project will showcase regional examples and UK expertise with a view to opening opportunities for international companies, including from the UK.

titles: Development of a climate finance hub to stimulate Mexico's low carbon economy
descriptions: This will create a climate finance hub to develop financial instruments to support Mexico's transition to a low carbon economy. The project will work with UK and Mexican private and public sectors to create new and replicable trading methodologies for Mexico's financial markets. These markets will then be able to interact more easily with the international financial markets.

titles: Support Mexican rule of law through implementation of criminal statistics audit model
descriptions: This project will develop a methodology to audit crime data in Mexico. This is the first methodological approach adapted to the local context. This model will allow evaluation of the quality and reliability of the crime data registry of common law offenses. This initiative prevents the government from manipulating criminal data and promotes transparency by avoiding high impact crimes being classified as minor offences. It also prevents the government from using strategies of underreporting and late reclassification.

titles: Improving the justice system in Mexico by strengthening the framework for public defenders
descriptions: Using UK expertise to improve the professionalism and autonomy of public defenders, strengthening the right to an effective defence and oral trial practice under the new adversarial system.

titles: Increasing financial inclusion across the poorest communities by piloting mobile financial technology in Mexico
descriptions: A pilot to provide financial inclusion in marginalised communities within Mexico's largest social development programme. The project will inform better public policy through providing an insight into the financial habits and needs of Mexico's most marginalised. As a secondary result, in the longer term, there will be a larger market size and an increased demand for financial services and products from international companies, including the UK.

titles: Mexico: Scoping opportunities in Jalisco and Nuevo Leon
descriptions: Scoping will identify current constraints and opportunities for future interventions in three strands of Mexico's Prosperity focus: Business Environment, Energy and Future Cities, in the Mexican regions outside of the capital.This will result in interventions tailored to deliver focussed primary benefit and as a consequence have the potential to also generate a secondary benefit - increased opportunities for international businesses.

titles: Promoting best practice sharing in deepwater oil and gas exploration and development in Mexico
descriptions: Showcase UK capabilities across the supply chain in developing oil & gas deepwater projects which Mexico is starting to carry out as a result of their Energy Reform programme. This will open up commercial opportunities for international companies, particularly those with experience in deep water projects throughout the whole supply chain.

titles: Prosperity Fund Mexico Business Case Development [now suspended]
descriptions: Activities related to development of the Mexico Business Case (including design, procurement, engagement and transition activities to smooth the path to the full programme) [now suspended]

titles: Promoting marine and run off river energy to increase energy diversity in Peru
descriptions: To inform Peruvian Government of potential for marine and run off river resources to further Peru's sustainable energy diversity and provide concrete recommendations for next steps, including use of UK expertise, leading to increased use of sustainable energy in Peru.

titles: Promoting investment in renewable energy in Peru
descriptions: This project will identify and address the legal and fiscal barriers to investment in renewable energy in Peru, map the potential for low cost, locally appropriate technologies, and specify pilot initiatives for quick implementation in rural areas, thus creating a market including for UK companies.

titles: Support increase in infrastructure development through use of Public Private Partnership methodologies in Peru
descriptions: To transform the planning, preparation, evaluation, project initiation and forms of PPP contract of Peruvian infrastructure programmes based on best practices, so that projects can be successfully brought to market, involving high-quality international (including UK) companies in the provision of necessary infrastructure development in Peru.

titles: Improve health standards in Peru by developing a National Blood Service pilot
descriptions: To show practically how a safe and adequate supply of blood components and related services could be made available in Peru, including using UK expertise, reducing mortality from a lack of blood in surgical and emergency facilities.

titles: Facilitating the distribution of household renewable energy technologies in Peru
descriptions: To increase clean energy usage in the Loreto region, Peru and develop income opportunities for Peruvians via a scalable pilot of a micro-distribution model for renewable energy technologies, including market-leading British brands, using a trained network of community agents. This will help enable low income families to meet their energy needs.

titles: Providing scalable solutions to energy access in rural areas in Peru
descriptions: To increase rural electification rates in remote areas of Peru by demonstrating a variety of off-grid applications for integrated solar energy storage systems, including those developed in the UK, providing a scalable solution to this barrier to economic development.

titles: Improving connection of Peru mobile healthcare facilities in rural areas
descriptions: To improve healthcare provision in remote areas via enhanced connectivity in mobile healthcare facilities. This will help to improve responsiveness, quality and range of services in poorer remote areas and allow patients and practitioners access to better medical information. The project will provide opportunities for UK and international business within the medical sector through the adoption of new health technologies.

titles: Improve Tuberculosis control in rural areas of Peru via mobile laboratories
descriptions: To deliver a portable TB laboratory to reduce TB prevalence in remote areas, and demonstrate effectiveness of this type of mobile clinic to meet Peru's rural healthcare needs.

titles: Developing a model sustainable home for low-income populations helping to tackle poverty in Peru
descriptions: Develop a model domestic dwelling that is safe, cheap and sustainable and can be deployed nationally to tackle a severe shortage of sustainable housing in Peru's poorer urban areas, including using UK innovation.

titles: Improving governance, quality assurance, leadership and internationalisation in Peruvian Higher Education
descriptions: Drive improvement in Peruvian Higher Education through technical assistance and training for the education regulator and upskilling researchers and leaders, including through building closer ties to world-class UK institutions.

titles: Support the regional implementation of Peru's national English Language Policy
descriptions: To increase Peru's competitiveness and capability through supporting the implementation of its national English Language Policy in different regions of the country, drawing on UK best practice, via the direct provision of training in the regions by UK experts.

titles: Transforming English Language Teaching in Peru
descriptions: Increase standards of English language education in Peru by developing a revised Initial Teacher Education programme for all Year 1 & 2 trainees and Year 3 English specialists, together with development of teacher Monitoring and Evaluation instruments for use in the school system, including showcasing UK expertise in this sector.

titles: Promoting energy efficiency and sustainability in Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) in priority sectors in Peru
descriptions: Delivery of a scalable pilot programme with clusters of Peruvian SMEs to identify key market failures and overcome known barriers around lack of awareness, access to finance and public-private collaboration in the provision of clean, sustainable energy solutions, increasing energy efficiency in Peru and providing opportunities for suppliers, including from the UK.

titles: Support technical education in rural Peru across Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education
descriptions: To increase demand in technological careers in Lima and Ica regions in Peru by delivering innovative and inspirational technology training based on STEM Education Programme to poorest and rural zones high school's students via the design, delivery and management of a mobile laboratory, based on UK expertise and promoting UK best practice.

titles: Ensuring a lasting legacy for Peru's PanAmerican Games
descriptions: The project will help ensure a social, economic and environmental legacy to the Lima 2019 Pan-American Games, drawing on UK knowledge and experience at London 2012 and Glasgow 2014. The project will help to ensure sustainable development and inclusive economic growth are outcomes from the delivery of a clearly articulated legacy vision. Opportunities will also be created for UK and international businesses.

titles: Improving heart disease diagnosis systems in Peru
descriptions: To make diagnosis of heart disease more accurate and cheaper for patients and doctors in Peru by introducing innovative, low-cost Magnetic Resonance Imaging diagnosis technologies and expertise from the UK.

titles: Supporting the Philippines to enhance transparency and integrity through increased reporting and evidence gathering of corruption
descriptions: The project aims to develop a crowd sourcing platform that utilises social media to encourage a wide reach of citizen engagement toward greater transparency through integrity pledges and incident reports of corruption, bribery and abuse of power. The generated reports provide evidence for the filing of administrative or criminal cases, leading to greater transparency and integrity in both public and private institutions.

titles: Supporting the delivery of a lower carbon and more secure energy future for the Philippines
descriptions: The will bring together a coalition of government and energy stakeholders to develop a sustainable energy policy roadmap that supports use of liquefied natural gas as an economic, energy-secure and low-carbon solution to the Philippines' increasing power demand, generating opportunities on LNG imports and infrastructure investments for international businesses, including UK companies in the sector.

titles: Supporting the development of a judicial framework for the Philippines' first National Competition Policy
descriptions: The project is designed to support the Philippines to set in place its first National Policy for Competition. Its successful implementation hinges heavily on setting the necessary judicial framework, developed through bilateral exchange between the Supreme Court of the Philippines and the UK counterpart competition agency, with training of relevant judicial bodies; thus levelling the economic playing field among local and foreign players through competitive policies in key sectors and boosting sustainable and inclusive growth in the country.

titles: Promoting economic growth in the Philippines by creating new mechanisms to increase business participation in Public Private Partnership projects
descriptions: The project is designed to, by 2019, promote the use of alternative mechanisms and an innovative framework to increase foreign investors' participation in Philippine infrastructure projects by at least P7 billion and make the Philippine PPP market more globally competitive, in view of the limitations on foreign equity ownership set in the Philippine constitution.

titles: Building capacity to reduce corruption and improve the business environment in the Philippines
descriptions: The project supports and builds the continued effective anti-corruption interventions by the Office of the Ombudsman that improve the Philippine investment climate and overall country competitiveness, particularly through capacity building workshops and development of official modules on standard practices involving investigation and prosecution of graft and corruption cases, in close partnership with the National Integrity Centre.

descriptions: Programme facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in India.

titles: Supporting Chinese innovation in business
descriptions: This project is designed to work with Chinese and UK stakeholders, to identify business-led innovation priorities to help address China's socio-economic challenges. This will support China's intention to move to a sustainable economic model led by innovation, in line with its Five-Year Plan, and will generate opportunities for international business, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of China's legal system to help improve the business environment
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to strengthen the process of legal and judicial reform in China in a manner that helps to promote the rule of law as well as improve the business environment. It will do this by developing a new UK-China legal and judicial cooperation mechanism which will enable both sides to address common legal and judicial challenges arising from economic development and the advance of technology. This will generate opportunities for international business, including UK ones in the legal and judicial sector.

titles: Promote understanding and cooperation in China of the UK's common law legal system
descriptions: This project is designed to promote understanding of the UK's common law legal systems and enhance legal cooperation with leading Chinese experts. This will advance the rule of law overall as well as enable a series of new specialist projects as part of a UK-led Rule of Law for Prosperity Programme. This programme will foster joint work with China that will support more sustainable national development and stable economic growth, generating opportunities for international business, including UK ones.

titles: Producing a scoping study for a rule of law programme in China
descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource for a Prosperity Fund programme on supporting and strengthening the rule of law in China.

titles: Supporting the development of China's international legal capacity
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance engagement with an increasingly influential community of Chinese international law scholars who are involved in advising the Chinese government on a wide range of international law issues. These issues include international trade law and international dispute settlement processes. This will improve the business environment in China, bringing benefit to international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the improvement of Chinese financing for infrastructure projects
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to help Chinese policy makers adopt improved methods for financing infrastructure projects This will generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting China to improve compliance with international and local standards in infrastructure investment projects.
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to help China improve compliance with international standards in infrastructure in third countries in China's One Belt One Road (OBOR) initiative. This will help create sustainable infrastructure in OBOR countries; and generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the delivery of vocational education in Ningbo, China
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to support the city of Ningbo to set up a framework to support the delivery of vocational education in two key priority skills areas – Advanced Manufacturing and Port Logistics. This will generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Promoting UK-China engagement to build China's workforce skills in visual and broadcast industries and China’s move to a sustainable economic model
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to help China reform its system of education qualifications and Continuous Professional Development in its visual and broadcast industries. It will support China's intention to move to a sustainable economic model led by innovation, in line with its five year plan, and is expected to generate opportunities in the education market for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Strengthening the enabling environment for financing and concession development in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on international best practice (including UK experience) to recommend ways in which China might strengthen its system of financing and concession in infrastructure work. This will also deepen awareness of the legal and regulatory environment among the development and reform commissions of local governments, entrepreneurs and other market participants.

titles: Promoting UK-China engagement to help the employability and skills of Chinese graduates, supporting China's move to a sustainable economic model.
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to help Chinese graduates enhance their employability and enterprise skills, including through online training and support. This will help drive economic growth in China, supporting China's intention to move to a sustainable economic model led by innovation, in line with its five year plan. This is also intended to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones

titles: Supporting the implementation of a national apprenticeship framework in China
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise in Technical and Vocational Education and Training to contribute to a national global standard apprenticeship framework in China, with enhanced competency based teaching and learning and industry engagement. This will support China's intention to move to a sustainable economic model led by innovation, in line with its Five-Year Plan, and will generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of entrepreneurial and networking skills in China
descriptions: This project is designed to implement a successful UK-China joint student enterprise pilot programme and recommend a strategy for broader roll-out and implementation. This will contribute to China's economic growth and strengthen relationships between the UK and China.

descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource for a Prosperity Fund programme on low carbon development in China.

descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource for a Prosperity Fund programme on developing a capital markets policy programme in China.

descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource to collaborate in the Chinese aerospace sector.

descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource for a Prosperity Fund programme on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths education in China.

titles: Fostering cooperation on infrastructure and utilities and their investment and financing by way of concession between China and UK (Part B)
descriptions: The project aims to will have strengthened Chinese knowledge of infrastructure investment and policy dialogues between the participants within the area of infrastructure and utilities, and their investment and financing by way of concession. It will establish and strengthen the related legal and market systems, improving the sustainability, quality and efficiency of public services, and promote steady and sustainable economic growth.

titles: Producing a Scoping Study for a China Sustainable Infrastructure programme
descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for use of future Prosperity Fund resource for a Prosperity Fund programme on creating a UK-China Sustainable Infrastructure Programme in China and third countries.

titles: Improving transparency and preventing corruption in public procurement in Thailand
descriptions: The project is designed to promote good governance, transparency, and a competitive business environment in Thailand by improving rules and regulations of government contracts and professionalization of public procurement personnel. It will create the first Thailand public procurement law that is also aligned with international practice as a result of close consultation with UNDP; and developing of a certification curriculum and sharing of lessons learned with other countries in Southeast Asia. It is expected that this will level the playing field for international businesses looking to invest, including UK ones.

titles: Strengthening the enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights in Vietnam
descriptions: This project is designed to increase the effectiveness of intellectual property rights enforcement in Vietnam, to reduce IPR infringements, deter production of and trade in counterfeit and to create a healthy business environment for enterprises. It will do this by enhancing the capacity of enforcement agencies; building the legal basis for Market Surveillance; strengthening the cooperative relationship between enforcement agencies and the private sector; increasing the cooperative relationship among relevant agencies; and increasing the awareness of enterprises and authorities.

titles: Improving the business investment environment in Vietnam through supporting the implementation of foreign arbitral awards
descriptions: The project is designed to enhance the capability of authorities and stakeholders in Vietnam, including its Ministry of Justice, to support Vietnam's effective implementation of the 1958 New York Convention on Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (FAAs) and increase successful recognition of FAAs generating opportunities for international business including UK companies. This will involve Vietnam establishing an Action Plan and a cooperating, collaborating and monitoring mechanism

titles: Promoting the application of international standards of business integrity in Vietnam
descriptions: The project is designed to promote the application of international business integrity standards to business associations and groups of businesses in Vietnam through the support for anti-corruption solutions and engagement with public and private stakeholders drawing on Transparency International's experience in promoting business collective action in other ASEAN countries, in order to help improve the business environment, including for international businesses in Vietnam.

titles: Supporting Vietnam to meet its international obligation in reducing green house gas emission in line with Paris Accord.
descriptions: The project will draw on UK expertise to provide hands-on technical support to the Vietnamese government over the next three years, by assisting the inventory compilation team and associated Ministries/Agencies to meet international climate change through the implementation of the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory System, as mandated by the Prime Minister, generating opportunities for low carbon investment from UK financial institutions and companies

titles: Supporting Southern-Vietnam Solar Photovoltaic Development to enable improved energy efficiency and reduced costs for business
descriptions: The project is designed to provide assistance and technical support for industrial and commercial businesses to increase rooftop solar capacity in Ho Chi Minh City, Binh Duong, Dong Nai, and Long An to 1,200kW by December 2018. This is expected to generate opportunities across the solar market for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of Vietnam's capital market and Public Private Partnership financing framework.
descriptions: The project is designed to support the development of financial markets in Vietnam through improvements in the policy and regulatory environment for government and corporate bonds facilitating both domestic and international investor participation (including the UK). It will improvd management of the Viability Gap Funding scheme, part of the Memorandum of Understanding between the UK government and Vietnamese Ministry of Finance and create a favourable business climate for companies operating in Vietnam. The Public Private Partnership framework will increase opportunities for UK companies to participate in large infrastructure projects and enhance quality and transparency of those projects.

titles: Supporting Vietnam to prepare the required legal frameworks to implement free trade agreements and benefit from trade liberalisation.
descriptions: The project is designed to improve Vietnam's trade and investment framework by reviewing it against the requirements of forthcoming comprehensive free trade agreements and providing comprehensive and accurate information on the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) trade policy. With a more liberal and AEC-integrated market, Vietnam will become beneficial destination and meaningful hub to AEC for UK trader and investors.

titles: Building the capacity of Small and Medium Enterprises to resist corruption in Vietnam
descriptions: The project is designed for a local anti-corruption education programme to provide Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) with practical means to strengthen their resistance to corruption, implement the best international compliance standards in their business operations, and develop opportunities for collective action, thereby encouraging competition, growth, and business confidence as well as opening up benefits and opportunities to UK companies that have SMEs in their supply chains.

titles: Strengthening the capacity of the Supreme People's Court of Vietnam in handling foreign commercial cases and requests
descriptions: The project is designed to strengthen skills in handling foreign commercial disputes and requests on enforcement of foreign court judgments and arbitral awards. It will provide training courses on international experiences and national provisions and dissemination of court precedents on international commercial disputes. Supporting the improved quality of resolutions on foreign commercial disputes and creating favourable conditions for foreign business communities (including UK business).

titles: Establish the use behavioural psychology to tack the culture of corruption in Latin America
descriptions: Using UK expertise from The Behavioural Insights Team, the project will look at areas of corruption in public services and construction sectors across three Latin American countries. It will work to reduce corrupt practices and strengthen processes throughout the supply chain. This will improve the playing field for international and British industries.

descriptions: The ASEAN Regulatory Reform Project is part of the ASEAN Economic Reform Programme. titles: Colombia PF Exit Costs
Colombia PF Exit Costs - covering projects in rail, agri tech, agri insurance and public procurement
descriptions:
Task 1.0 Rail Development (exit costs)
This project developed a National Rail Regulatory Framework for Colombia. This framework will allow and enable public and private operators to create a more sustainable transport system that will support the existing and future demand requirements, whilst also supporting Colombia’s drive to de-carbonise its economy. agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
The presence of elevated concentrations of certain naturally occurring elements in drinking water tube wells can and has caused significant adverse human health effects, affecting the health and well being of millions of people in developing countries. Most widely known is perhaps the case of  arsenic in drinking water bores in Bangladesh and arsenic and fluoride in other ODA countries especially across SE Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. 
Manganese is the latest element for which there is a growing and deeply concerning body of epidemiological evidence indicating adverse effects on human health. For example, [1] calls for an re-evaluation of international guideline values for manganese in drinking water because of associations with neurological symptoms. Specifically for Bangladesh, [2] concluded that children are at risk for manganese-induced neurotoxicity and preliminary findings from [3] indicate a possible association between manganese exposure and infant mortality. 
In response, developing countries need to rapidly develop manganese mitigation strategies to reduce exposure where elevated levels are detected in drinking water. This requires input from three key disciplines: biogeochemistry, water treatment engineering, and robust measurement technology.
A manganese mitigation strategy is needed for Bangladesh. This project has the aim of developing a roadmap to this manganese mitigation strategy. This will be achieved through establishing collaboration between relevant expertise in the UK and Bangladesh and co-creating the roadmap with stakeholders in Bangladesh.  This agile research base will also allow the team to respond to further ODA funding calls. 
[1] Wasserman et al 2006. Water Manganese Exposure and Children’s Intellectual Function in Araihazar, Bangladesh. Environmental Health Perspectives, 114(1), 124-129.
[2] Ljung & Vahter. 2007. Time to re-evaluate the guideline value for manganese in drinking water?. Environmental health perspectives, pp.1533-1538.
[3] Hafeman et al. 2007. Association between manganese exposure through drinking water and infant mortality in Bangladesh. Environmental Health Perspectives, pp.1107-1112.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
This proposal is focused at tackling the fundamental challenge of water quality monitoring by both developing new sensing platforms and optimization algorithms to maximize the overall effectiveness of the monitoring system. The activity is based on two main pillars: development of novel microsensors for measuring concentration of chemicals (pollutants), and development of an algorithm to optimally place the sensors to maximize the collected quantity of information.  Microcantilevers will be fabricated with a suitable coating to facilitate the attachment of molecules of interest on their surface. Such microcantilevers will be put in oscillation using a recently proposed self-excitation loop [Torre et al., Nanotechnology, 24, 325104 (2013)] and the change in mass due to the attached molecules will be detected via shifts in the oscillation frequency. The use of self-excitation will allow achieving much larger signal-to-noise ratio with respect to traditional externally excited sensors.
Moreover, a tailored spatial optimization routine will be developed to find the strategic positions for the sensors that allow the overall system to collect the maximum amount of information about the pollution process, e.g. location and intensity of the source. Such algorithm will be tested in an ad-hoc realistic simulator based on real geographical and hydrological data of a river in Brazil, which represents a typical scenario where the envisaged sensor platform will be used. The long-term vision is to mount the developed sensors on autonomous platforms (e.g. surface vessels or underwater vehicles) so that their location can be dynamically changed according to the evolution of pollution process.
A workshop to showcase the results of this pilot project to relevant academic community and local stakeholders will be organized at the end of the project at the University of Campinas. Such event will also represent an opportunity to finalize plans for future collaborations and joint funding bids.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
The quality of water for swimming, during Rio Olympic 2016, was discussed several times. Although, for the period of the Olympic, these issues were temporarily resolved but they alarmed Brazilian urban and water managers and planners about their severe water contamination challenges. 
São Carlos is located on the geographic center of the São Paulo state in Brazil. The city has an active industrial profile with important national and international industries and certain agricultural importance. Due to its increasing number of high technology industries, the city has been proclaimed "The National Capital of Technology" by Brazilian President in 2011. However, these fast growing urban development, industrialisation and agriculture have caused severe water and environmental contamination in the whole city. On the other hand, lack of efficient and appropriate wastewater treatment system have exacerbated the contamination challenges. These contaminations have put a great risk to the health and wellbeing of the people and aquatic ecosystems. Promotion of resilience to water quality stresses and crises is a necessity in Sao Carlos. This resilience promotion requires development and enhancement of the knowledge and capacities to manage the emerging challenges and risks. Currently, a detailed and integrated map of active and potential contaminators across the city, is lacking.  
The long-term vision of this research is to contribute to resilience promotion in Sao Carlos by developing a dynamic information platform for water quality monitoring and assessment. The current research aims to initiate this long-term plan by developing an integrated GIS map of the contaminators and contaminated areas in Sao Carlos. These maps could be used for water quality spatial and temporal analysis. Also, they will enable the local and national decision makers to proactively respond to water contamination across the region. Furthermore, these maps could be used for integrated urban wastewater system asset management plans.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
The world has met the UN’s Millennium Development Goal of halving the proportion of people without access to improved water sources, with over 2.6 billion people gaining access since 1990 [1]. However, studies have suggested that the quality does not always comply with WHO recommended guidelines with 38% of improved “safe” sources observed to have faecal contamination [2]. One limiting factor is the availability of an effective water filtration system that does not require high-energy inputs, lengthy filtration time or expensive consumable filters. 
In developed countries, membranes are already employed for water filtration both in large centralised plants and in smaller units for remote communities. These solutions are however, problematic in ODA countries. Polymeric membranes have high-energy requirement and require high-pressure to perform efficiently. In developing countries where there is no grid it is really challenging to generate pressure consistently in order to operate such systems. Moreover fouling of the materials decrease the performance of the membrane over time and requires mechanical or chemical cleaning. If the system is not properly maintained, there is a high risk of water contamination and the lack of technical knowledge of the local population could lead to a false security.
In order to overcome the above limitations, we propose a novel water filtration system based on highly dense, nanoporous (diameter 50nm-100nm) membranes. The proposed system will bring about several advantages over existing solutions including; i) high selectivity to bacteria; ii) high permeability to water; iii) low energy requirements, and, iv) fouling avoidance and reusability. Silicon is the material of choice for this first proof-of-concept prototype due to its chemical, mechanical and thermal stability. Finally, a large breadth of micro-/nanofabrication processes have already been developed for Si, mitigating the fabrication risk and providing us with unprecedented control in tailoring the properties of the fabricated membranes.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
China’s population is aging rapidly - this pace of population aging is much faster than many other high-income or low and middle-income countries.  In the next 25 years, the percentage of people in China aged 60 years or over is expected to more than double, from 12.4% in 2010 to 28% in 2040.  The rural population has a higher proportion of older people due to rural-urban migration, with many older people left behind in rural areas.
Falls are a major cause of mortality and morbidity among older adults, and have become one of the most common health problems. Globally, more than one in four people aged 65 years or over have at least one fall per year.  In China, falls are responsible for more than two thirds of all injuries in people aged 65 and above.  Falls prevention has been identified as a major governmental priority in China.
We aim to provide a risk prediction tool based on machine learning for use in rural, poor regions of China to allow elderly villagers at risk of falls to be identified (and subsequently involved in prevention strategies such as behavioural and physical training).  This project will collect physiological and medical data from 480 volunteers from 12 villages in rural China (Ningxia Province), and then follow-up those patients at 3 and 6 months to identify which have suffered falls.  The resulting data will be used to construct a prototype of a validated risk prediction tool, which will be deployed in a smartphone environment for use in follow-on work in which the system would be scaled-up for assisting healthcare workers in rural settings.  China Mobile will support both the implementation and the scaling-up of this work; the Oxford team will construct the model, while the George Institute team will undertake the study.

We seek to combine novel disposable microfluidics tools with state-of-the-art portable microscopy tools to help deliver a platform for early and point-of-care antibiotic susceptibility testing in the developing world. A number of common bacterial diseases – such as urinary tract infection (UTI) and gonorrhea – and a lack of strongly enforced regulations lead to unnecessary prescription of wide spectrum antibiotics. In fact, the vast majority of antimicrobial prescriptions are made outside the hospital, by doctors without using a diagnostic tool, by pharmacists or by self-medicating patients buying antibiotics over the counter (OTC). In the broader context, the problem is also related to potable water contamination with waste and human excreta, which is a common problem in resource starved countries. Current, long established methods for bacterial water contamination and infection diagnosis take place in clinical laboratories using bacterial cultures, which introduce a substantial time delay – certainly not ideal for resource starved developing countries. A need for a novel, point-of-care (POC) and rapid antibiotic susceptibility and diagnostic tool is thus evident. In the current seed proposal, we seek to develop engineering solutions for POC antibiotic susceptibility testing, with plans to develop a diagnostic tool through future work.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
In many developing countries, local decision makers at city or district level have a crucial role in meeting sustainable development goals, including clean energy and sustainable cities. If they fail to propose and enact effective regulation and policy, these sustainable development goals will not be met, and countries will not be able to meet their Paris Agreement obligations. However, local decision makers often do not have the capacity or technical knowledge to make sense of the complex systems in which they operate and the evidence that is available to them to make decisions. 
In industry, decision makers have adopted decision support systems, which can analyse and visualise complex systems to give insights and optimise decisions. In this project, we will investigate how this technology can be used to empower local policy makers to optimally use the information available to them in order to further sustainable development. We will focus on the city of Surat in Gujarat, India, which is starting a rooftop solar energy programme, and work with council-level decision makers to develop a Proof of Concept for a decision support system based on the industry-standard BOXARR platform, populate this system with data on the technical and economic parameters of and constraints on solar energy and its alternatives available at UoE and TERI, assist local users, and evaluate effectiveness and scalability of this technology and its practical, technical and social constraints.
This will enable local stakeholders to evaluate options and provide Surat with clean energy and a sustainable city at the lowest cost, but more importantly, it will generate knowledge about the use for and constraints on evidence-based decision support systems to local decision makers in developing countries; paving the way for future extensions of this technology to other areas, cities and countries.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions: Photovoltaic (PV) panels are the most common means to harvest solar energy – the most abundant renewable energy source - and convert it to electricity. Due to dust accumulation, solar cell efficiency can drop by about 40% within a year in a dusty climate. Cleaning PV panels by traditional approaches damages the cell surfaces and consumes large quantities of water – this exacerbates the water scarcity issues, in particular in water starved western India and Sub-Saharan Africa, which are attractive locations for solar energy. The water consumption also adds costs to the cell maintenance. Therefore, there is an urgent need for novel cleaning approaches that avoid surface damage and the massive water loss – the solution of this problem clearly has direct energy and environmental benefits. One possible solution is to exploit self-cleaning superhydrophobic and transparent coatings. If designed properly, droplets on these surfaces can roll-off smoothly at minor tilting (<10 degrees) of the surfaces. The rolling drops can collect the dust particles with them, thereby facilitating energy-efficient cleaning with relatively smaller amounts of water. The current project seeks to introduce scalable, spray coated and transparant superhydrophobic coatings as a water saving dust mitigation strategy for PV cells.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

descriptions:
Developing indigenous remote energy engineering lab solutions to address all-important educational challenges faced by most of the developing countries including India. It is the first step and many innovations fail to achieve an impact due to their inability to expand beyond their local environment. 
India has the installed capacity of power generation is more than 300 GW and it is estimated to increase up to 800 GW by 2030 with the aim of providing electricity to 61% of household. But to achieve this target a large team of skilled persons is required.
International Energy Agency has prioritised knowledge economy through the energy policy, to promote the solar energy education for sustainable development. It is a bigger engineering challenge to promote solar systems without appropriately educated people who will be involved in their design, sizing and installation.
University of Kota in Rajasthan is the only university in Rajasthan, to offer Masters course in Solar Energy, but they do not have laboratory facilities. In this proposal we use Internet of things to address the challenges in training skilled people, students and teachers in developing countries through remote solar lab. 
This project aims for the development of an open access remote PV laboratory for educational purposes. The remote PV lab will consists of specialised PV equipment, sensors, monitoring and control hardware, will be installed outdoor at our facilities of the Open University, allowing the users from Indian Institute to perform real tests and experiments with photovoltaic panel using Internet of things.
 A remote laboratory offers the ability to perform an extensive set of educational experiments under real conditions through the Internet. At the same time, the student can have a live view of the systems through a camera, offering him/her a sense of personal presence in the place where the experiment takes place.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions: We are addressing the challenge of testing water quality in India. Our goal is the delivery of an accurate and reproducible digital water testing device based on microfluidic and mobile phone technology. The aim is to provide low-cost easy to use pathogen detection in a portable system capable of use on-site. Our application is the performance characterisation of decentralised water treatment technologies, in stream systems that complement centralised treatment systems, thereby allowing for mobile deployment and rapid adaption of waste water treatment with population growth. At present the first field testing of an existing decentralised water treatment system is in place and this proposal aims to explore methods and technologies to improve the existing decentralised water treatment technology, bringing together an interdisciplinary team spanning the fields of water treatment, microfluidics, sample concentration, paper colorimetric based detection technologies and big data analytics. Furthermore, the water testing device is more widely applicable and when fully automated could be employed to assist in the management of centralised water treatment systems, enabling rapid feedback to users to adjust parameters for enhanced performance. The main activities will be knowledge exchange between the partners and the organisation of a workshop with local stakeholders to fully understand the requirements of the end-users. The key outcome will be generation of detailed device requirements and pilot data to enable a larger funding application.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
The unprecedented population growth in the cities of developing countries has put immense pressure on the existing wastewater treatment infrastructure. As a result, large quantities of untreated and partially treated wastewater flows in open storm drains. These flows have led to the contamination of surface water bodies. The recent incidents of large scale fish kills, foam formation and fire in Bangalore lakes have put immense pressure on the policy makers to address the issue of wastewater flows into water bodies. This critical issue requires solutions that would address both monitoring & treatment of water before it finds its way into the waterbody. Through the integration of bio-electrochemical systems (BESs) and instream treatment systems (STRAins) we propose to address both challenges. The core idea is to use the local flora to treat wastewater and generate electricity which would provide power to the real time water quality monitoring systems. This project will integrate multiple disciplines such as biology, electrochemistry, engineering, urban planning, social science and education to address the water quality issues in Bangalore city. We propose the following set of activities under this project 
• Visit of an Indian team (PI) from ATREE to Cambridge University  to understand the pros and cons of BES systems
• Visit of the team from Cambridge(PI) to familiarize with the water quality issues in the Bangalore city
• Integrating the STRains systems with the BES systems in the lab at ATREE in Bangalore and plan experiments to assess the feasibility of the integrated system. A member of the team from Cambridge will spend few weeks in Bangalore.
• Organizing workshops to disseminate the knowledge and get feedback on the feasibility of integrated systems from the concerned policy makers, scientists and civil society groups.
• Visiting local Schools/colleges and educating the next generation engineers and scientists.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

The Fellowship targets two of the Global Challenges Research Fund priority areas, namely health and sustainable agriculture, and aims to develop a novel miniaturised biomedical imaging technology in collaboration with developing country partners. The collaboration will include implementing a research and application framework for the new imaging technology with partners in India and UK/international collaborators. Specific applications of this technology for “neglected” tropical infectious diseases (e.g. Leishmaniasis) and crop science are envisaged through a collaborative optimisation and application with a partner in India. The low-cost imaging technology will enable the investigation of drug resistance in Leishmaniasis, a debilitating disease which primarily affects developing countries. The proposed imaging technology will integrate two of the newest biomedical imaging modalities, namely selective plane illumination microscopy (SPIM) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI) into a miniaturised 3D-printed package. Further application of the technology is also expected in neuroscience and cancer research.
SPIM allows rapid optical sectioning and real-time 3D fluorescence imaging with very low light doses which avoids cell-damage. PAI is based on sensing of optically excited acoustic waves, which embeds information on localized micro-mechanical cell/tissue properties and cell/tissue dependent contrast. The novel combined implementation of SPIM and PAI in a miniaturised 3D-printed form will enable more comprehensive insight to be gained into biomedical functional processes, while reducing the required equipment size (from ~1m3) and cost (from ~£50,000) by 1-2 orders of magnitude. 
The combination and miniaturisation in a small scale (centimetre range with millimetre parts) 3D-printed system will be achieved through integration of MicroElectroMechanical System (MEMS) active mirrors, micro-optics and optical ultrasonic transducers. Miniaturisation advantages of portability and implementation flexibility will be enabled through an optical fibre based source delivery and light collection. This can lead to the multiplexing of large numbers of similar systems and drastically reduce the cost per system.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions: Sand-dams are a widely used low-cost-low-tech water treatment and storage technology creating artificial aquifers for both storage and biofiltration of river water. Sand-dams are sub-optimal in their engineering design and the fundamental physical, engineering and biological basis of their operation are uncharacterised.  While sand dams are promising low technology solution to water storage and purification in developing countries, there is to-date insufficient evidence to support the building of more sand dams.  Here we propose an interdisciplinary approach to deliver the first comprehensive inventory of the microorganisms associated with water quality provided by three sand-dams in eastern Kenya over a complete dry season (May to August 2017).  As with all biofiltration technologies, it is the microbiology driving water treatment processes. Ironically, while the biology can deliver water quality, it is also responsible for system and water quality failures.  It is therefore imperative to understand the microbiological quality of the water produced via sand-dam treatment and the contribution of microorganisms to this processes. Through this understanding, improved sand dams can be engineered intensify the biology to deliver improved operation, and thus improved water quality. Here we bring together expertise in engineering geology, civil engineering and environmental microbiology to provide a detailed molecular inventory of microorganisms, including potential pathogens associated with sand-dam water, that will contribute to the first comprehensive assessment of the water quality derived from sand-dams.   This represents the first-step towards understanding the complex processes controlling water quality, which the researchers hypothesize are similar to the processes used in slow sand filtration. In addition, it will provide a sound foundation on which evidence based decision can be implemented on the usefulness of sand-dams as low-cost, low-tech solutions for improved water quality.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions: Developing indigenous engineering solutions to address developmental problems across Sub-Saharan Africa is just the first step and many innovations fail to achieve an impact due to their inability to expand beyond their local environment. Considerable challenges can be encountered when growing the distribution network of technologically advanced products. The Nanofilter®, developed by Dr Askwar Hilonga, is a highly sophisticated product and its distribution and management requires an ecosystem of advanced knowledge and skills. Any distribution partner needs to have water quality testing capability, business entrepreneurship skills as well as a capacity to conduct community engagement and education programmes. In Tanzania, the Nanofilter distribution system benefitted from the support of the Nelson Mandela - African Institute of Science and Technology (NM-AIST), so this project will assess the viability of using a University-centred network as a means to enable access to the Nanofilter across Sub-Saharan Africa. This proposal includes a pilot study, involving two academic institutions in Kenya; the Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST), in Kakamega and Oshwal College (OC) in Nairobi. The pilot study will test the viability of setting up one Nanofilter distribution centre at each University in Kenya, the centres will target one case study community each and establish a network of Water Stations involving local entrepreneurs. The water stations will then facilitate Nanofilter distribution to community households. Plymouth University (PU) has expertise in developing entrepreneurial networks in East Africa and will oversee the case study exercise, assist in the project evaluation and help to disseminate lessons learned. The project will include quantitative and qualitative methods to collect data that will enable the assessment of the University-centred system. Lessons learned about leveraging indigenous African innovations through University-centred organisation networks will be disseminated via a workshop event, held at the end of the research programme.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
Many low income countries have little local product development or manufacturing capability and poor infrastructure drives up the cost of imported goods, putting them out of reach of the poorest (Tech for Trade, 2016). This lack of local manufacture has a direct impact on a country’s Gross Domestic Product and hinders growth and development.
To combat this global challenge many initiatives have been implemented to provide a low cost / intermediate technology to enhance the living standards of those in poverty (Er, 1993). However, there is a growing school of thought that suggests instead of providing substandard equipment and products, government and non-government organisations (NGOs) should instead be investing in game changing technologies which utilise rapidly increasing cellular networks and internet connections seen across the world (UNICEF, 2017). 3D printing is one such technology which provides a real opportunity to leapfrog highly capital intensive manufacturing seen in developed nations and begin to bridge the divide between the two. For example; a remote village in Kenya would no longer need to depend on unreliable transportation networks, but instead could use a local 3D printer to print both basic and advanced parts, such as; complex components for agriculture tools, or spare parts for a water filter, which would improve their livelihood and productivity (3D Print, 2015).
This project seeks to develop capacity within the Kenyan market for 3D printing, by highlighting the benefits of this technology, supporting local 3D printer manufactures and developing ten product case studies. The project will culminate in a Launch event will be held at Nairobi University to demonstrate the added value of digital manufacturing and the role it can play in business. The event will be an opportunity to promote designers, engineers and digital artisans in Kenya and showcase the work they can achieve locally manufacturing products.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions: The number of amputees in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) is un-proportionally high compared to the western world. Some countries suffer the adverse legacy of previous conflicts, such as uncleared landmines in Sri Lanka. Researchers and non-profit organisations have addressed this challenge exploring 3D printing technology to create low-cost body-powered prosthetic upper limbs. Several notable attempts have shown that these type of prosthetic devices may be possible. However, the initial investment of 3D printers in local communities and the lack of knowledge in LMICs on how to operate and maintain these fabrication systems create challenges in delivering the expected impact. The aim of this project is to address this challenge and develop a prosthetic hand, made of low-cost, recyclable and accessible materials available in the local environment in the LMIC.  Based on our recent research working closely together with LimbForge and the Enable Community Foundation (non-profit organisation who developed the first 3D printed body-powered upper limbs), we will run a student competition to manufacture the best-designed prosthetic hand from low-cost material and develop a series of videos and protocols for local people in need. All participating teams will be advised throughout by clinicians from developing countries (i.e. Sri Lanka). The best design will be chosen towards the end of the project. The winning team will visit Sri Lanka for two weeks working with local hospital/amputees to improve their design, share knowledge, deliver and validate the prosthetic hand engaging with local amputees. We strongly believe that in this way a body-powered prosthesis made of locally available, low-cost, recyclable material will make a difference and deliver the impact that amputees in LMICs are desperately waiting for.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.

titles: Frontiers of Engineering for Development
descriptions:
In many rural communities in Mexico, access to safe drinking water is still a luxury. In this country, groundwater is the main source of drinking water. Its intensive and unregulated extraction to meet the demand of a growing population, is, however, the cause of severe soil sinking and cracking. In addition, over 70% of the superficial and underground waters available is heavily polluted, due to the lack of basic sanitation and the direct and indirect (e.g. pipe leaks) discharges of domestic, industrial and agricultural wastes.
Our vision is to bring together expert researchers in the area of water security provision, along with local NGOs, government bodies and water companies, to generate a country-wide view of water resources and pollution hotspots that can support the development of effective management and resilience strategies for the public good.
To achieve such vision, we have assembled a multidisciplinary team from the University of Bath, University of Bristol and the Mexican non-governmental organisation (NGO) GO Fomento Mexicano, which, by focusing on the rural community of Llano Grande as an initial case study will: 1) collect and interpret historic crowd-based data on the distribution of water resources; 2) identify pollution sources and monitoring locations; 3) engage with the affected community and interactively disseminate the impact of water mismanagement and direct waste discharge; 4) develop a collaborative network with researchers from Mexican universities, such as Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM) and El Colegio de México, and key stakeholders, such as environmental agencies and water companies; 5) design an interactive website, available to the citizens, for the open-access and user-friendly release of the monitoring data gathered.
This programme will contribute to the engineering research base focussed primarily in the developing world and also play a capacity-building role.
